text: Ask one question in class.
why: Even if your voice does that weird squeak. Especially then.

text: Give someone a specific compliment.
why: Not “nice shirt.” Tell them exactly what you noticed.

text: Try one bite of something unfamiliar.
why: Your taste buds deserve a plot twist.

text: Sit near someone new at lunch.
why: You do not have to become best friends by dessert.

text: Name the feeling you are actually having.
why: Upgrade “fine” to one more honest word.

text: Say “I don’t understand yet.”
why: Confusion is allowed. Pretending is exhausting.

text: Text someone you have been meaning to check on.
why: Four words work: “Hey, how are you?”

text: Join something for ten minutes.
why: A game, a club, a conversation. You can reassess at minute eleven.

text: Take three slow breaths before replying.
why: A dramatic pause, but useful.

text: Share an idea before it feels perfect.
why: Rough drafts are allowed to leave your brain.

text: Learn how to pronounce someone’s name.
why: Ask, listen, try again. Names matter.

text: Do one thing without asking if it looks cool.
why: Dance. Draw. Wear the socks. Survive the scandal.

text: Turn off your phone for twenty minutes.
why: It will miss you terribly. It will recover.

text: Disagree without making it personal.
why: Try: “I see it differently because…”

text: Invite someone who might be left out.
why: Make the circle one person wider.

text: Attempt the hard version first.
why: One honest try. You can switch modes after.

text: Write down one thing you handled well.
why: Your brain keeps receipts for mistakes. Add a better one.

text: Ask for help with one real thing.
why: Specific is good: “Can you show me the first step?”

text: Say thank you—and include the reason.
why: Tell them what their help changed for you.

text: Start before you feel ready.
why: Two minutes counts. Momentum is sneaky.

text: Replace one mean self-joke.
why: Talk to yourself like you are on your own team.

text: Tell a friend what you need.
why: No mind reading required: “Could you just listen?” works.

text: Introduce yourself first.
why: Name. Smile. Tiny leap. Done.

text: Wear or carry something that feels like you.
why: Even if it earns one raised eyebrow.

text: Let one small mistake stay unhidden.
why: Correct it if needed. Skip the five-minute apology tour.

text: Say “no” to one thing you do not have room for.
why: A full sentence is optional. A boundary is not rude.

text: Repair one awkward moment.
why: Try: “That came out wrong. Can I try again?”

text: Show someone something you made.
why: No pre-apology. No “it’s bad, but…”

text: Choose a second impression.
why: Notice one new thing about someone you judged too quickly.

text: Stand up for someone in a small, safe way.
why: Include them, interrupt a joke, or get a trusted adult.

text: Ask someone what song they have on repeat.
why: Listen to the answer. Bonus brave: play the song later.

text: Volunteer an answer before you are completely sure.
why: Certainty is not an entrance requirement.

text: Take a different route through a familiar place.
why: Keep it safe. Let your routine be mildly surprised.

text: Write one worry and circle the part you can control.
why: The rest can sit outside the circle for a minute.

text: Introduce two people who might get along.
why: Human bridge. Very small infrastructure project.

text: Ask one real follow-up question.
why: Go one step past nodding like you understood everything.

text: Practice a skill you avoid for five minutes.
why: Being bad at minute one is extremely normal.

text: Put your phone out of reach for one whole task.
why: Not face-down. Actually out of reach. Bold.

text: Send a voice note to someone you miss.
why: Your unedited voice counts as a complete message.

text: Correct one wrong assumption about you—kindly.
why: Try: “Actually, that’s not quite me.”

text: Do one small thing alone you usually wait to do with someone.
why: A library table, a snack, a short walk in a safe place.

text: Let an awkward silence last five seconds.
why: Do not rescue it. Count slowly. Notice that everyone survives.

text: Thank someone whose work is usually invisible.
why: Notice the setup, cleanup, fixing, carrying, or remembering.

text: Share your opinion before checking everyone else’s.
why: Your first thought is allowed into the room.

text: Make something with a material you normally ignore.
why: Tape, cardboard, voice memo, mud. Tiny laboratory rules.

text: Leave one nonessential thing unfinished overnight.
why: Perfection can sleep outside for once.

text: Ask someone older what they were like at your age.
why: Adults had awkward phases. Important historical evidence.

text: Admit one small mistake without explaining it away.
why: A clean “that was me” is enough.

text: Be the first person to start a group task.
why: Open the document. Move the chair. Say the first sentence.

text: Name one useful thing your body did today.
why: Breathing counts. Carrying you around definitely counts.

text: Offer help before someone asks.
why: Carry one thing. Hold one door. Make one task lighter.

text: Say “I need a minute” instead of faking an answer.
why: A pause can be more honest than a fast yes.

text: Practice where someone can see or hear you for five minutes.
why: Let the rough draft be publicly alive.

text: Choose rest before you have completely earned it.
why: Rest is fuel, not a prize at the bottom of the tank.

text: Ask someone to teach you one small thing.
why: A knot, a shortcut, a word, a recipe. Be teachable.

text: Ask for one specific piece of feedback.
why: Specific question. Useful answer. Less mysterious doom.

text: Enter a room without checking your phone.
why: Look up. Arrive on purpose.

text: Celebrate what is finished before naming what needs fixing.
why: Good work gets one full sentence before the critique arrives.

text: Tell someone what you appreciate about how they think.
why: Compliment the mind, not just the result.

text: Change the subject when a group conversation turns mean.
why: A small redirect can be a quiet rescue.
